description: CAPT-SPEC 2026-07-12 (v4.0.0) — partMass_g now comes from a DRAWING THAT EXISTS. Until today this recipe demanded SOLL 10.35 g with toleranceSource 'drawing', and there was no drawing: erp.articles.gewicht_kg was NULL for all 222 articles, qms.characteristics carried no injection-moulding characteristic at all, and the recipe itself admitted the bands 'mirror the housing-A SOLL' — an article that does not exist in the 222-article master. Meanwhile machine.ts drew part masses as normal(partMassTargetG, 0.8 %), zero-mean noise about the machine's own config constant, so the machine's true mean was exactly 10.40 g. The celebrated Ca of 0.147 was thus the distance between a sim constant and a typed number, wearing a provenance that pointed at nothing. --- WHAT IS TRUE NOW. The part sgm-004 actually runs is _V4_12-0044-003 ("Steckergehäuse Typ C"), and it already had a RELEASED drawing in the PLM (DWG-12-0044-003) whose content column was NULL. The place existed; it was empty. It now holds the geometry, and the band below is DERIVED from it: cavity volume 7.936 cm3 x 1.36 g/cm3 (PA66-GF30, ISO 1183) = 10.79 g nominal, and the limits [10.31, 11.27] are NOT a second typed number — they are the drawing's wall-thickness tolerance (2 +/- 0.1 mm) propagated through the same volume formula. Because the number now comes from the product's geometry, toleranceSource 'drawing' finally RESOLVES: windchill.documents -> DWG-12-0044-003. The band is BINDING and may not be widened to make a deviation vanish — widening it would mean re-drawing the part. --- THE MACHINE STILL DEVIATES, AND NOW FOR A REASON. The sim no longer carries a magic mass offset. It moulds the cavity (7.936 cm3) and the melt is PACKED: part mass rises with holding pressure, which is exactly why a setter weighs parts to dial Nachdruck in. sgm-004's mould is a USED tool, and the sim's own wear model already raises the pressure as a tool ages (wearPressureFactor, machine.ts) — so the machine packs above the design point and every part comes out ~0.9 % heavy. Small, physical, and invisible: 100 % of parts stay INSIDE the drawing band while the process centre is off. That is the product's whole claim, and it is now earned rather than staged. --- SEPARATION OF KINDS: partMass_g is a PRODUCT characteristic (drawing, binding). mouldTempC is a RESIN property (norm, binding). The pressures / hot-runner / cushion are MACHINE SETTINGS from the process data sheet (process_estimate, optimisable) and are passed through here untouched. Throwing all three into one file under one 'drawing' stamp is what produced the fiction we just removed. --- CAPT-REGIME 2026-07-29, TWO THINGS MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE THAT THIS FILE USED TO GET WRONG. (1) THE GATE. mouldTempC carried no `gate` here between 9d50b52 and today, and that was not a decision this file was able to make: the operative guard lives on profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json#recipe_mould_temp_band (`when: inCycle==true`), which is what it-evaluator copies into the spec and what edge-api turns into its interval CTE. `parameters[].gate` has no consumer at all. So the removal changed nothing except what this file CLAIMED, and the claim was false for 17 days. The guard is restored here as a mirror, and ci/lint-recipes.mjs now fails the build if the two ever disagree again. Keeping the guard is also the substantive answer: the profile's own measurement says an idle SGM reads exactly 25.00 degC ambient, so an ungated mouldTempC band would raise a deviation against a recipe that is not running. What CAPT-WINDOW believed would replace the gate — `population` excluding the cold data BY CONSTRUCTION — does not happen; see (2). (2) THE POPULATION IS DECLARED AND DORMANT. Every band above declares scope current_regime with on_change [mouldId, resin]. Measured over the full retained history on the live edge (7 d, 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-29): mouldId changed 0 times, resin changed 0 times. The edge honours the declaration and answers `regime_start: null` — 'NO declared marker has ever fired' — so the population IS the full history, and the live Golden answers are computed over all 599,522 hotrunnerTempC and 11,842 partMass_g samples. The declaration is CORRECT and it is signed; it is simply not yet doing any narrowing, and it will not until this machine is re-tooled or re-materialled. It is left exactly as it is: the alternative marker that does move, currentProgram (1,871 changes in the same 7 days), is a job number and not a process regime — declaring it would drop partMass_g to 23 samples, under min_sample_n 1000, and trade two working verdicts for two evidence gaps. --- 2026-07-31 WAVE-3, hotrunnerTempC SOLL 230 -> 295 degC. The 230 in this file was never this machine's setpoint. sgm-004 is an Engel victory 120 running PA66-GF30 and its configured nozzle setpoint IS 295 degC (sim-v5 packages/machines-sgm/src/config.ts:337 — barrelSetpointsC [270,282,290,295], nozzleSetpointC 295); the simulator DERIVES the resin FROM that setpoint (resinForNozzleTemp(), config.ts:257-261: >=268 -> PA66) and couples it to the part-mass model, so 295 is the intended truth and lowering the machine to meet this band would corrupt the simulation. hotrunnerTempC is published per cavity as nozzleC + normal(0, 1.5) (machine.ts:1281-1283), i.e. N(295, 1.5^2) in steady state. MEASURED by the consumer 2026-07-31: mean 295.0, range 289.9-300.5 over 6277 samples in 2 h — a textbook fit to N(295,1.5) at +-3.7 sigma, and 65 degC above the 230 this file used to demand, so EVERY judgement on this signal was against a number nobody aims for. Both bands are re-centred on 295 with their EXISTING half-widths PRESERVED: the temp band keeps +-6.5 -> [288.5,301.5] (+-4.33 sigma, Cp = 13/(6*1.5) = 1.44 >= cp_min 1.33, and it contains the measured range with margin), the control limits keep warn +-3.5 / action +-4.5 about SOLL-0.5 -> warn [291,298], action [290,299] (action = 3 sigma, which is what an Eingriffsgrenze is supposed to be). NO width was widened to buy silence — only the centre moved, and the centre is the machine spec. Temp-band upper 301.5 and action upper 299 both stay inside the equipment envelope [180,310] raised in the same wave (equipment_hotrunner_temp_envelope). toleranceSource stays 'process_estimate': this is a machine setting off the process data sheet, not a drawing number.
